finding.claim: Negative amount on /transfer lets an authenticated user take funds from any existing account: the attacker is credited and the victim debited.

trace.note: amount read from request body with no sign validation
BAL[g.user] < amount is False for amount=-X, so no abort

finding.guards_checked: Balance check at line 11 is upper-bound only. No amount>0 check (contrast /withdraw line 21), no type check, no recipient-existence check. Precondition: caller authenticated as g.user (see AUTH-1). Severity HIGH: cross-user financial loss. Validation Tier 0; repro POST /transfer {"to":"victim","amount":-100}.

verdict.guard_found: None on the /transfer path. bank.py:11 is an upper-bound-only balance check (BAL[g.user] < amount), and bank.py:10 and :14 have no sign, type, or recipient-existence checks. The amount>0 check exists only in /withdraw (bank.py:21), not /transfer.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: bank.py:10 reads amount unvalidated, bank.py:11 passes for a negative amount, bank.py:13 credits the sender, and bank.py:14 debits the recipient. Any caller who can reach /transfer as an authenticated user can trigger this, and no control on that path blocks it. Caveat: g.user is never assigned in the repo (only bank.py is present, with no auth middleware), so the authentication precondition is assumed rather than verified here.

finding.claim: NaN or Infinity amounts corrupt balances and disable the insufficient-funds guard, permanently destroying the recipient's funds.

trace.note: BAL < NaN is always False, so the check never aborts
recipient balance becomes NaN; subsequent < guards in /transfer and /withdraw never fire

finding.guards_checked: No finiteness or type validation on amount. Relies on Python json accepting NaN/Infinity by default with Flask request.json; exact Flask version not verified. Severity HIGH: cross-user destruction of funds. Validation Tier 0; raw body {"to":"victim","amount":NaN}.

verdict.guard_found: none. bank.py:10 takes request.json["amount"] with no type or finiteness check. The only check, bank.py:11 `if BAL[g.user] < amount: abort(400)`, is false for NaN, so it never aborts. For Infinity it passes too, since the balance is finite. /withdraw at bank.py:21 has the same gap: `amount <= 0` is false for NaN, and `BAL[g.user] < NaN` is false. Flask's default JSON parsing (stdlib json.loads) accepts the NaN and Infinity literals, and this file sets no custom app.json decoder.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: bank.py:10 takes amount from the JSON body unchecked, bank.py:11 never aborts for NaN, and bank.py:13-14 write NaN into both balances, so any authenticated user (g.user, set outside this file) can send {"to":"victim","amount":NaN} and corrupt the recipient's balance; the only caveat is that g.user's auth setup is not in the provided code, which affects who can reach the route but not whether the flaw is effective.

finding.claim: Check-then-debit is not atomic, so concurrent transfers or withdrawals can overdraw accounts and create value across accounts.
finding.source: Concurrent HTTP requests to /transfer or /withdraw by the same authenticated user
finding.sink: Balance write BAL[g.user] -= amount (bank.py:13 and bank.py:23) and credit BAL[to] += amount (bank.py:14)

trace.note: balance read and compared to amount
separate, unlocked debit; two requests can both pass line 11
recipient credited for each request, so one debit yields two credits

finding.guards_checked: No lock, transaction, compare-and-swap, or idempotency key. Flask threaded default makes concurrent handlers reachable. Validation Tier 2 (race under production concurrency); severity HIGH because it produces negative balances and value creation.

verdict.guard_found: none. bank.py:11 and bank.py:21 are bare comparisons whose result only gates abort(400). Nothing between the check and the debit (bank.py:13, :23) or credit (bank.py:14) takes a lock, transaction, or compare-and-swap. The only other file in the directory is a skill doc, so no lock or auth code exists in the codebase.
verdict.reason: The check at bank.py:11 and the debit at bank.py:13 (and :21/:23 in withdraw) are separate, unlocked read-modify-write steps on the shared BAL dict, so concurrent requests from one user can both pass the check and overdraw, with lost debits producing extra credits at bank.py:14. The attacker is an authenticated user, since g.user is required, but g.user is set outside this codebase, so the authentication step is unseen; the race itself is Tier 2 (narrow window, depends on production concurrency), so the severity should reflect that.

finding.claim: Debit happens before credit, so a transfer to an unknown or unhashable recipient debits the sender and then fails, destroying the funds.
finding.sink: BAL[g.user] -= amount (bank.py:13) followed by BAL[to] += amount (bank.py:14) raising KeyError or TypeError

trace.note: KeyError (unknown key) or TypeError (unhashable) raised; HTTP 500 with no rollback and no credit

finding.guards_checked: No recipient-existence check, no type check on to, no rollback or atomic apply. Harm falls on the sender, so MEDIUM; platform totals no longer reconcile. Validation Tier 0; repro POST /transfer with to=nonexistent amount=10.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only checks are the balance test at bank.py:11 and the amount check at bank.py:21, and neither validates `to`. Nothing wraps lines 13-14 in try/except, a transaction, or a rollback. In BAL[to] += amount (bank.py:14), an unknown key raises KeyError and an unhashable value raises TypeError, both after the sender debit at bank.py:13 has already been applied.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: bank.py:13 debits the sender, then bank.py:14 raises on a missing or unhashable `to` with no rollback, so the sender loses the amount (bank.py:13-14). Any caller who can reach /transfer can trigger it, but the loss falls only on the caller's own balance, so this is a self-inflicted integrity bug rather than a privilege issue, and the candidate's MEDIUM rating fits.

finding.source: Unlimited repeated requests from an authenticated client to the public routes
finding.guards_checked: No limiter decorator or middleware in the file. No gateway rate-limit config in the repo, so infrastructure-level limiting cannot be ruled out. MEDIUM (payment/transfer endpoint).
